COVID-19 proteome response across two sample matrices

Olink reanalysis: differential expression, cross-matrix concordance, severity structure, and data quality

Author

Elisa Marquez

Published

September 15, 2026

Summary

At a pre-specified FDR of 5% (no effect-size filter), 210 of 436 proteins differ between COVID-positive and negative samples in the plasma subcohort (170 up, 40 down in COVID) and 209 in the serum subcohort (201 up, 8 down). 145 proteins are significant in both matrices, and 100% of them move in the same direction. Across all 436 shared assays, fold changes correlate at Spearman ρ = 0.80.

The two matrices tell one biological story: the acute COVID response (interferon signaling, cytokines, endothelial activation) dominates in both, with serum showing systematically larger effect sizes (regression slope serum ~ plasma = 1.58).

Data and methods

Data. Two Olink sample matrices from the same study: a longitudinal plasma subcohort (307 samples) and a serum subcohort (63 samples), each measuring 436 proteins across five panels (CM, CVD2, CVD3, Inflammation, Immune Response). Negative (control) samples in the plasma subcohort are dialysis patients – chronically inflamed relative to healthy donors – which compresses observed effect sizes.

Preprocessing. Protein x sample matrices were built per subcohort from the harmonized long table. Pre-specified missingness rule (identical for DE, PCA, and heatmaps): proteins with >20% missing values are dropped (none were, in either matrix); remaining gaps are median-imputed per protein. Values are Olink NPX (already log2 scale).

Differential expression. Linear models per protein (limma) contrasting COVID-positive vs negative. The plasma design accounts for repeated individuals via duplicateCorrelation (estimated intra-individual correlation r = 0.617). P-values are BH-adjusted across 436 tests.

Dimensionality reduction. Sample-level PCA on per-protein z-scores (proteins standardized across samples, so PCs reflect correlation structure rather than raw NPX abundance).

Data quality. Missingness is enumerated per assay and per sample (encoded as absent source rows); outliers are screened as Euclidean distance to the own-group centroid in PC1-PC5 (robust z, one-sided, threshold 3); plate x group balance is tabulated. QC flags are informational – no samples are excluded (no pre-specified exclusion rule).

Results: differential expression

With the effect-size filter applied, 97 plasma and 173 serum proteins clear both display thresholds. Down-regulation is rare and weak – consistent with an acute inflammatory state sitting on top of a chronically inflamed control group.

Results: cross-matrix concordance

Of 210 plasma and 209 serum hits, 145 are significant in both matrices – and every shared hit points the same way (100% direction concordance). Serum fold changes run systematically steeper (slope 1.58), consistent with its controls sitting closer to baseline.

Results: PCA and severity structure

Sample-level PCA (per-protein z-scores; PC1 captures 19.1% and PC2 8.9% of variance in plasma) separates COVID-positive from negative samples along PC1 — standardized separation of 1.05 SD (Cohen’s d) in plasma, and similarly in serum (25.6% on PC1).

In plasma, PC1 does not merely separate disease from control — it grades with severity. Mean PC1 by category:

Mean PC1 by severity category, plasma subcohort
Severity n mean_PC1
NEGATIVE 51 7.0
mild 73 4.6
moderate 62 -0.9
severe 74 -2.3
critical 47 -10.0

Mean PC1 score by severity category (plasma). Boxes: median, IQR; points jittered.

The same dose-response is visible in the top-DE proteins: in the category-average heatmap, up-regulated proteins deepen monotonically from NEGATIVE through critical, and down-regulated proteins reverse.

Top-50 DE proteins, mean per-protein z-score per category. Left bar: DE direction. Plasma categories are severity levels; serum falls back to Group (no severity annotations available).

The per-sample heatmap (307 columns for plasma, with Group/Severity column annotations) is best explored interactively in the app’s Heatmap tab.

Data quality

QC summary per subcohort. All values computed live from qc.rds artifacts.
Subcohort Samples Assays Missing cells % missing Assays >20% Samples >20% Outliers Plates
Plasma 307 436 275 0.21 0 0 6 5
Serum 63 436 97 0.35 0 0 0 1

Missingness is trivially low overall — 0.21% of plasma cells and 0.35% of serum cells — and concentrated in three plasma samples with complete single-panel dropouts:

Samples C10_6, C189_345, C224_361 each lost one entire panel (CVD2, CVD2, IR — 87 assays each; all other panels fully observed). Each sits just under the pre-specified 20% threshold (19.95% missing) and is retained under the fixed rule; together they account for 261 of the 275 missing plasma cells (95%). Affected values are median-imputed per the preprocessing rule. QC flags informational; no samples excluded (no pre-specified rule). A sensitivity re-run excluding these three samples is listed as future work.

Outliers. The within-group screen (Euclidean distance to own-group centroid in PC1-PC5, robust z (median/MAD), one-sided) flags 6 plasma samples (C65_11, C27_240, C24_211, C10_47, C99_299, C11_237; all POSITIVE) and none in serum. Flags are informational.

Plates. Plasma controls are spread across all 5 plates by design (~10-11 per plate), so plate cannot confound group:

Serum is a single plate, so batch QC is not applicable there. LOD flags not computable: LOD fields absent from the harmonized dataset.

Limitations and future work

Limitations.

  • Control group. Plasma negatives are dialysis patients – chronically inflamed relative to healthy donors – so observed effect sizes are conservative (compressed toward zero). Direction of change is robust; magnitudes are not comparable to healthy-baseline studies.
  • Serum power. The serum subcohort has 11 negative samples (of 63 total), so serum-only findings carry wide uncertainty.
  • Unbridged matrices. No Olink bridge normalization links the two subcohorts; every statistical test is within-matrix. Cross-matrix statements are qualitative (direction concordance, rank correlation) – not quantitative equivalence of effect sizes.
  • No LOD information. LOD flags not computable: LOD fields absent from the harmonized dataset.

Future work, in priority order:

  1. Severity contrast DE (severe vs mild among positives; bins of 74 vs 73): the PC1 dose-response and category heatmap strongly suggest severity effects will replicate at the DE level.
  2. Sensitivity re-run excluding the three full-panel-dropout samples – a one-line change to the pipeline inputs, then diff against the current de_results.rds.
  3. LOD-aware QC once limit-of-detection fields become available.

Reproducibility. Every number and figure in this report is computed at render time from the committed pipeline artifacts (outputs/<subcohort>/{de_results,pca,heatmap,qc}.rds); nothing is transcribed by hand. Pipelines live in R/run_*.R (harmonize → DE → PCA → heatmap → QC); the companion Shiny app serves the same artifacts, so report, app, and data cannot drift apart.
